summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), with a B.E. in Electronics and Telecommunication from the University of Mumbai. Built bare-metal C firmware on ARM Cortex-M4 (STM32) with interrupt-driven ADC and I2C sampling, and used FreeRTOS with mutex-protected task coordination for real-time multi-servo control. Designed and validated UART, I2C, SPI, and PWM sensor and actuator interfaces on an oscilloscope and logic analyzer, and led PCB design and sensor integration for a 25-member competitive robotics team.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers over I2C with a Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF motion into real-time HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and interrupt-driven sampling resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware integration end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in bare-metal C with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with no HAL/RTOS overhead; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination between a Jetson vision node and an STM32 motion controller communicating over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over I2C for range gating, with real-time OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated, contact-aware grasp control.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for camera range-gating and gripper contact detection.
Debugged and resolved 11 integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, false-positive detections); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
